source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which teaching is correct for a client wearing a Holter monitor?
options: Keep an activity and symptom log
questions.rationale: The client records activities and presses the button with symptoms, avoids electrical devices and showers, and wears loose clothing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Holter Monitor (PDF p. 68)
questions.quote: Instruct the client regarding recording and pressing the button upon experiencing pain or discomfort

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How long does a Holter monitor usually record?
questions.rationale: The Holter monitor records cardiac activity continuously for 24 hours during normal activities.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Holter Monitor (PDF p. 67)
questions.quote: Records electrical cardiac activity on a continuous basis for 24 hours

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before an exercise stress test, the client should:
questions.rationale: NPO 4 hours, avoid tobacco and caffeine, and wear exercise clothes and rubber-soled shoes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Stress Testing (PDF p. 68)
questions.quote: NPO 4 hours before the test

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which condition contraindicates a stress test?
questions.rationale: Contraindications include unstable angina, severe aortic stenosis, acute myocarditis, severe hypertension, and heart failure.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Stress Testing (PDF p. 68)
questions.quote: Unstable angina

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After cardiac catheterization, how is the head of the bed kept?
questions.rationale: Bed rest 2–6 hours with HOB no greater than 30°; check the site and distal pulses.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Catheterization (PDF p. 69)
questions.quote: Head of the bed no greater than 30 degrees

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After cardiac catheterization, which assessment of the affected leg is frequent?
questions.rationale: The extremity's temperature, color, and capillary refill and peripheral pulses are checked often.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Catheterization (PDF p. 69)
questions.quote: Temperature, color and capillary refill of the affected extremity are frequently evaluated.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a radioactive iodine uptake test, what should the client do?
questions.rationale: Flush immediately after each voiding, wash hands well, and increase fluids for 24 hours.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Radioactive Iodine Uptake (PDF p. 70)
questions.quote: Flush toilet immediately for three times after each voiding

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug may DECREASE radioactive iodine uptake results?
questions.rationale: Lugol's solution, SSKI, antithyroid drugs, and antihistamines may decrease results; lithium, estrogen, and barbiturates may raise them.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Radioactive Iodine Uptake (PDF p. 70)
questions.quote: Drugs that may decrease results. Lugol's solution, SSKI, anti-thyroid, antihistamines

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A high TSH with low thyroid hormone suggests:
questions.rationale: TSH increases in primary and congenital hypothyroidism; it decreases in Graves' and excess replacement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, TSH Assay (PDF p. 71)
questions.quote: Primary hypothyroidism

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before a 24-hour urine VMA test, which food should be avoided?
questions.rationale: Avoid amine-rich foods (bananas, avocados, chocolate, coffee) and vanilla for 48 hours; VMA tests for pheochromocytoma.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, VMA Test (PDF p. 71)
questions.quote: Avoid foods high in amines for 48 hours (bananas, avocados, beer, aged cheese, chocolate, cocoa

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The VMA test helps diagnose which condition?
questions.rationale: VMA, a metabolite of epinephrine, helps diagnose pheochromocytoma, neuroblastoma, and ganglioneuroma.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, VMA Test (PDF p. 71)
questions.quote: Assist in the diagnosis of neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma or pheochromocytoma

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should a client prepare for an OGTT?
options: Regular diet 3 days, then NPO 8–12 hours
questions.rationale: Eat a regular diet at least 3 days before, be NPO 8–12 hours, and avoid smoking.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, OGTT (PDF p. 72)
questions.quote: Take regular diet for at least 3 days before the test

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Glycosylated hemoglobin reflects glucose control over about how long?
questions.rationale: HbA1c reflects blood glucose levels over up to 3 months.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Glycosylated Hemoglobin (PDF p. 72)
questions.quote: Reflects serum glucose levels up to 3 months

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the normal fasting blood glucose range?
questions.rationale: Normal FBS is 70–110 mg/dL after 8–12 hours NPO.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fasting Blood Glucose (PDF p. 72)
questions.quote: Normal: 70 — 110 mg/dL

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What should the client do right before paracentesis?
questions.rationale: The client voids before paracentesis to avoid bladder puncture and sits upright.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Paracentesis (PDF p. 72)
questions.quote: Void before the procedure

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After paracentesis, which finding is a priority to watch?
questions.rationale: Watch for hypotension and hypovolemic shock from fluid shifts; measure girth.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Paracentesis (PDF p. 72)
questions.quote: Observe for hypotension and hypovolemic shock

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During needle insertion for liver biopsy, the client should:
questions.rationale: After several deep breaths, the client exhales and holds at end-expiration while the needle is inserted.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Liver Biopsy (PDF p. 73)
questions.quote: Instruct client to resume breathing after the physician aspirates and withdraws the needle

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before a liver biopsy, what must be available?
questions.rationale: Coagulation tests and compatible donor blood are confirmed because of bleeding risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Liver Biopsy (PDF p. 72)
questions.quote: Ascertain that results of coagulation tests and compatible donor blood are available

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After liver biopsy, which activity is avoided for one week?
questions.rationale: Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity for a week; avoid coughing and straining early.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Liver Biopsy (PDF p. 73)
questions.quote: Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity for one week

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the normal serum albumin level?
questions.rationale: Normal serum albumin is 4.0–5.5 g/dL; total protein 7.0–7.5 g/dL.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Protein Studies (PDF p. 73)
questions.quote: Serum albumin 4.0 - 5.5 g/dL
